what: decimal (round(x,2)) and printed Moth Number (round(x*100)) disagree by 0.01 on ties.
how: Verified (ruin=0.25 gave 0.03 vs M0.02). The printed string now derives from the stored rounded decimal (_pct = round(round(_dec,2)*100)); this only makes two already-intended paths agree, the stored decimal and every score are untouched, and the audit's scan of all 244 live ASSAYS rows found 0 mismatches so no live row changes (Hard Rule 3: not a scoring change).

what: Parseable-but-empty GROUNDINGS.json ({} / [] / null) read as ok and was published as all-ungrounded.
how: Verified. _load_groundings now returns ({}, False) unless the document is a non-empty dict, so both existing refusals in main() (rc 2) fire. Did NOT add the audit's second half (count-of-grounded compare against the standing TIERS.json, SHRINK_FLOOR style): a threshold is a curatorial number, so it is left as an option for the owner. Bootstrap (missing file) behaviour unchanged.

what: --write publishes a smaller GENRES.json (or {}) with rc 0 when records are skipped.
how: Verified. Before writing, main() compares against the standing GENRES.json: if this run classified nothing, or any source the standing file has is missing, it names every dropped source (uncapped), refuses to write and returns 1. Sources never classified (the 6 empty-entries records) are not refused. Not run against live tree. Side effect: a source legitimately removed from the roll now needs its GENRES.json row removed by the owner before --write lands.

what: Misspelt / absent shelf name reported as DISCONNECTED.
how: Verified. main() checks --from/--to against the graph first, prints 'NOT IN GRAPH: <names>' and returns 1 without searching.

what: Zero-byte .corrupt file graded 'zero bytes' though KEPT_DAMAGED_EXT says it must never be a red row.
how: Verified. Zero-bytes exemption now covers TRANSIENT_EXT + KEPT_DAMAGED_EXT; plain zero-byte .json still a fault.

what: A second torn ledger/samples file overwrote the first .corrupt.
how: Verified. New _wreck_path(path): <path>.corrupt if free, else <path>.<epoch>[.n].corrupt (still ends .corrupt so estate recognises it); used by both the ledger and samples preservation branches. The fresh-ledger 'ledger:unreadable: 1' count is unchanged.

what: Denied replace leaves the pid+thread temp file behind.
how: Verified. The denial arm now os.remove(tmp)s (noting on failure) before returning 1, as render.write_views does.

what: Stale line-number citations (assay.py x4, health.py x2, tiers.py x1).
how: Verified all. Re-cited by symbol in comments only (no code change): assay.py 226/1131/1578/1903, health.py 85 and 94 (the 'proposed to escalation.py:248' wording now says subject= is passed through), tiers.py :143 -> `_cut`.

what: check_state calls P.records() once per failed-synthesis source (whole-corpus read each time).
how: Verified by reading. Now one pass over P.records() against a set of failed sources (first record per source, same semantics as the old next()); memory stays flat. Timing not measured; net asserts the pass count no longer grows with the number of failed sources.

what: A self-test key's sample ring landed in _SAMPLES and state/failure_samples.json.
how: Verified. record() keeps the sample only when the key is not a rehearsal (same partition as the counts). No caller in src/ or drill.py reads _SAMPLES for drill keys.

what: write_views draws one sample node per tier and main uses WS.build_all(limit=1); is that the intended product under Hard Rule 0?
how: Options: (a) keep as a deliberate specimen page and rename/label it so; (b) render every node per tier (large output, needs a size/paging design). Owner ruling; carried from 67/16 Q3 (order 5bb12b398783). Not changed.

what: Default scan and --reachability return 0 whatever they find, including NOT MEASURED and UNDECLARED unreached lines.
how: Options: keep rc 0 (drill ratchets the count and is the enforcer) or return non-zero for NOT MEASURED. Changing rc alters what the supervisor/allsweep treat as a failure, so owner call.

what: dead_module reports 6 modules nothing names (descending_ladder, halo, module_index, pantheon, scale_theories, zfighters); module_index.py is documented as hand-run.
how: Options: put hand-run tools in EXEMPT_MODULES (empty today) with a written reason each, or leave them in the finding count. A curatorial decision about which modules are intentionally unreferenced.

what: terminal() husk test (len(body) < 64) covers .js only; a truncated non-empty PANSCRIPTUM_TERMINAL.html passes.
how: Options: add a closing-tag / minimum-size check for the .html, or accept since artifacts() catches zero-byte files. Needs a decision on what a valid terminal page must contain.

what: No halt interlock in tiers.main, genre --write, render.write_views (standing owner-routed class question 67/12 Q7).
how: Unchanged and not re-filed as a fix: options are to import health._assert_not_halted-style fail-closed interlocks in each writer, or rule them exempt. Owner ruling.

what: Genre cue stems over-match (hell/hello, ration/rational); carried from 67/03 Q3.
